statement: Top-1% wealth share at 2027Q4 >= 2025Q4 + 1 pp (Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts, 2027Q4 release)
status_at_phase_end: 2025Q4 is the baseline quarter and was not published within 2025. In-phase DFA releases put the Bloc A top-1% net-worth share at ~30.8-31.0% (Q4 2024, Q1 2025) and ~31.0-31.1% (Q2 2025, released late Sept 2025), a series record, driven by equity gains in which AI-linked stocks were prominent. Q3 2025 data (31.6-31.7%) appeared only in Jan 2026 after shutdown delays. Trend ~+0.4-0.5 pp/yr 2023-2025; a +1 pp rise over two years would need a faster pace than the recent trend unless equity gains continue. Vintages revise by ~0.1-0.3 pp.

items.summary: DFA update for Q4 2024: top-1% share of Bloc A household net worth 30.8% as first published, unchanged from Q3 2024.
items.detail: Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts via FRED WFRBST01134, vintage updated 2025-03-21 (Wayback capture 2025-03-26): Q4 2024 30.8, Q3 2024 30.8.

items.summary: DFA update for Q1 2025: top-1% share 30.8%, down from a revised 31.0% in Q4 2024.
items.detail: Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts via FRED WFRBST01134, vintage updated 2025-06-20 (Wayback capture 2025-06-30): Q1 2025 30.8, Q4 2024 31.0 (revised).

items.summary: DFA update for Q2 2025: top-1% wealth reached a record ~$52 trillion, ~31% of household net worth (record share); top-1% wealth rose ~8.5% y/y vs ~6.3% for the bottom half, driven by stock-market gains.
items.detail: Federal Reserve DFA following the 2025-09-11 Z.1 (household net worth $176.3T). CNBC 2025-10-03 'The wealth of the top 1% reaches a record $52 trillion'; Sherwood News 2025-10-06. Current-vintage 31.1%.

items.summary: Aggregate Bloc A household net worth rose to $176.3T in Q2 2025, with corporate equities +$5.5T - the main driver of top-share moves.
items.detail: Federal Reserve Z.1 Financial Accounts, Second Quarter 2025 (2025-09-11).

items.summary: The Q3 2025 DFA update was delayed by the federal shutdown and appeared only in Jan 2026; the 2025Q4 baseline was first published in 2026. The DFA is also re-benchmarked to each triennial consumer-finance survey (2025 wave), so the baseline value may be revised before resolution.
items.detail: Bloomberg/Forbes Jan 2026 report Q3 2025 at 31.7%; SCF 2025 fieldwork in 2025, results 2026. Single-jurisdiction series; no quarterly equivalent for Bloc B.
